pr_body:
Previously all the SubjectPublicKeyInfo decoders were specific to a key
type. We would iterate over all them until a match was found for the correct
key type. Each one would fully decode they key before then testing whether
it was a match or not - throwing it away if not. This was very inefficient.

Instead we introduce a generic SubjectPublicKeyInfo decoder which figures
out what type of key is contained within it, before subsequently passing on
the data to a key type specific SubjectPublicKeyInfo decoder.

Fixes #15646

issue_context.title: Decoding SubjectPublicKeyInfo structures is very inefficient
comments: IMO we should have wildcard decoders that can produce different key types based on the decoded data. The wildcard keytype decoder would be used in case the keytype is NULL instead of this _try every possible decoder_.
How would the wildcard keytype decoder work with keytypes it doesn't know?

> How would the wildcard keytype decoder work with keytypes it doesn't know?

Set the data type to be the OID in text form if it can't find the name.  In other words, a call to OBJ_obj2txt().  This is, incidently, what I do in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/15498/files#diff-9c8cda6982e26bbb9ca5a45076c49b4f0d61fa06051412c56f3e8813402a0ec5

There could be multiple wildcard decoders present. A third party wildcard decoder could be able to decode these. Of course that would still mean some inefficiency because presumably our wildcard decoder would be tried first and it would fail because it would not know the key type and then the third party one would be tried after that.
Using @levitte's OID idea, then we can have just one that knows what to do even in the case of an OID it doesn't recognise.
